xlg06_rookie_prior_stage1_rb.notes: WP46 dedicated follow-up on the secondary RB read flagged in the QB write-up (xlg06_rookie_prior_stage1_qb's notes field). Population/predictor/outcome/statistic/reliability method identical to the QB cell, position swapped to RB, via scripts/xlg06_rb_stage1.py which imports scripts/xlg06_rookie_prior_cfb_screen.py's functions UNCHANGED. --mode screen reused the original script's own RB seeds (cohort 4000, player 4100, reliability cohort 1001, player 1101) and reproduced its already-computed RB numbers exactly (r=0.06443485228551912 to 1e-6, matched by tests/test_xlg06_rb_stage1.py). Player-blocked secondary coherence check: r=0.06443 (same point estimate), CI [+0.00438,+0.12327], P+ 0.98175 -- agrees with the cohort-blocked primary. Per-cohort trend (13 individual cohort years, player-blocked within-cohort, descriptive only): 12 of 13 cohorts read positive point estimates (only 2013 negative, r=-0.090), only 2022's own CI sits entirely positive [+0.0457,+0.3660] and every other single cohort's own CI crosses zero -- MORE consistent across cohorts than the QB cell's per-cohort trend (which ranged -0.215 to +0.259 with no consistent sign). Positive-control (leaked monotone rank-transform of rating as the outcome) drove Pearson r to 0.9690 (cohort) / 0.9690 (player) and Spearman rho to 1.0/1.0, P+ 1.0 both blockings -- confirms the bootstrap machinery correctly reports a strong effect when one is engineered, but this is a code-path sanity check only, not sized to the real ~0.06 effect, so it is never cited as this cell's closing ground. This is Stage-1 CFB-only evidence about whether an RB usage prior is worth building at Stage 2 (crosswalk + NFL join, unbuilt); it is not an NFL claim.
xlg06_rookie_prior_stage1_rb.plain_summary: Does a recruit's star rating predict how much a true freshman RUNNING BACK actually plays in college?
